meta.title: HK416 D14.5RS action and recoil simulation
meta.model: lumped-parameter; see README.md for the physics, sources and limits
meta.frame: metres, +Z muzzle, +Y up, +X shooter's left, origin on the bore axis at the upper receiver front face (as hk416.glb)
meta.time_zero: sear release (trigger break); ignition follows at events.ignition
meta.units: seconds, mm / deg / MPa / N / m/s as each key says

nodes.note: hammer and firing pin are not modelled (only hammer_pin_l/r); their curves are for timing and audio

m_charge.note: M855: 26.1 gr WC844 (US Army TM 43-0001-27); varies by lot

m_case.note: fired 5.56 brass case with primer cup, about 95 gr

bullet_base0.note: bullet base from the bolt face when chambered (57.4 mm overall, 23.1 mm bullet)

chamber_vol.note: case capacity behind the seated bullet

port_to_muzzle.note: gas block centre to barrel crown in hk416.glb (photo-derived, not a published port position)

force_const.note: propellant force (impetus), typical double-base ball powder

gamma.note: ratio of specific heats of propellant gas

flame_temp.note: adiabatic flame temperature; sets the gas constant R = F/T0

form_theta.note: form function psi = (1+th)Z - th Z^2; negative = progressive (deterred ball grain); solved for the manual muzzle velocity

burn_exp.note: pressure exponent of the burn rate

burn_coeff.note: vivacity dZ/dt at 100 MPa; solved for the manual chamber pressure

loss_factor.note: heat loss to the bore as a fraction of the work done on bullet and gas

gas_velocity_conv.note: SAAMI free-recoil convention: propellant gas leaves at 4,000 ft/s (high-power rifle)

blowdown_scale.note: scale on the lumped blowdown thrust so total gas momentum equals the SAAMI convention (the raw lumped figure is kept in validation)

p_ign.note: primer/igniter pressure that starts the charge burning

p_shot_start.note: bullet pull and crimp release pressure

p_engrave.note: extra engraving resistance, decays over engrave_len

p_friction.note: bore friction as an equivalent pressure

brake_beta.note: momentum recovered by the muzzle device; the HK "compensator" is a flash hider, taken as 0

trigger_pull.note: 4.6 to 6 lb (20.5 to 26.7 N), midpoint; not used in the dynamics

hammer_inertia.note: about 33 g hammer, 22 mm radius of gyration about its pin

hammer_torque_cocked.note: hammer spring torque on the sear

hammer_torque_fired.note: hammer spring torque resting on the firing pin

hammer_fall.note: rotation from the sear to first contact with the firing pin

hammer_eff.note: fraction of spring torque left after pivot friction

hammer_strike_r.note: hammer pin to the face that strikes the firing pin

hammer_overcock.note: how far the carrier holds the hammer below the sear

fp_float.note: free travel of the floating pin before its tip meets the primer

fp_protrusion.note: firing pin protrusion 0.90 to 1.10 mm (p. 17): the hard stop on indentation

primer_fire_indent.note: indent at which the priming mix initiates

primer_delay.note: primer initiation to flame in the charge (start of the ballistics model)

port_d.note: barrel gas port diameter; solved for the target cyclic rate

cyclic_target.note: midpoint of the manual 700 to 900 rpm (p. 7)

piston_d.note: piston diameter, from the 9.8 mm piston tube in the model

vent_open_x.note: piston travel at which the cylinder vents

leak_area.note: leakage past the three piston rings

rod_stop_x.note: travel at which the piston rod stops and the carrier runs on alone

cyl_heat_eff.note: fraction of inflow enthalpy kept (wall heat loss)

m_carrier.note: carrier with cam pin, firing pin and retaining pin (AR-pattern scale)

m_bolt.note: bolt head with extractor and ejector

m_buffer.note: HK buffer with tungsten granules (weight not in the manual)

m_spring_eff.note: one third of the buffer spring

stroke_contact.note: carrier travel at which the buffer meets the tube end (AR pattern, about 3.75 in total)

buffer_restitution.note: low because the tungsten granules deaden the rebound (manual p. 5 names them)

battery_k.note: carrier to barrel extension contact stiffness (overdamped, zeta 2: no bolt bounce)

rail_friction.note: sliding friction of carrier, buffer and hammer drag

cam_dwell.note: carrier free travel before the cam track starts turning the bolt

cam_len.note: carrier travel over which the bolt turns

bolt_angle.note: AR-pattern bolt rotation between locked and unlocked

lug_r.note: mean radius of the locking lug faces

case_head_area.note: 9.6 mm case head: bolt thrust per unit chamber pressure

case_wall_area.note: case body wall bearing on the chamber

case_mu.note: brass on steel during primary extraction

cock_x.note: carrier travel by which the hammer is fully cocked

case_r.note: case body radius (9.6 mm head, 9.0 mm body)

port_front_z.note: front edge of the ejection port in build.py

feed_pick_bolt_x.note: bolt travel at which the bolt face meets the top round on the return

feed_free_x.note: carrier travel at which the round is clear of the feed lips

feed_friction.note: drag of stripping the round from the lips

sear_trip_x.note: carrier travel at which the auto sear is tripped on closing

hold_open_x.note: carrier travel at which the bolt catch holds the bolt after the last round

ejector_energy.note: ejector spring: 22 N compressed to 13 N over 2.8 mm

case_cm.note: centre of mass from the case head

eject_release_deg.note: case rotation about the extractor claw at release

eject_elev_deg.note: upward tilt of the ejection plane

deflector_deg.note: deflector face normal, from straight out (-X) towards the muzzle (+Z)

deflector_e.note: restitution of brass on the deflector

brass_cd_area.note: drag coefficient times mean projected area of a tumbling case

eject_height.note: ejection port above the ground for a standing shooter (trajectory samples only)

m_magazine.note: HK steel 30-round magazine (about 250 g) with 30 rounds

cyclic_rate.source: HK manual p. 7 (port diameter calibrated to the 800 rpm midpoint for the shouldered gun)

lock_time.source: Wikipedia "Lock time": mil-spec AR-15 and HK416 fire control about 10 ms (likely a calculated figure)

hammer_energy.source: No. 41 primer all-fire about 48 in-oz (commonly quoted; inferred relevance)

primer_indent.source: HK manual p. 17 firing pin protrusion

port_pressure.published: no HK figure; AR carbine-port figures of 90 to 180 MPa are quoted for a port 45 mm nearer the breech

recoil_impulse.source: SAAMI free-recoil formula with 4,000 ft/s gas velocity

free_recoil.published: about 4 to 5 J for 5.56 rifles of 3.2 to 3.6 kg (recoil tables, e.g. Chuck Hawks .223: 4.3 J at 3.6 kg)

carrier.published: no HK figure; AR carrier speeds of 4 to 6 m/s are commonly quoted

chamber_pressure_at_unlock.note: residual bore pressure while the bolt turns and when extraction starts

events.note: seconds after sear release, one semi shot, shouldered

auto.note: auto fire: the carrier trips the auto sear on closing; period is sear release to sear release

firing.note: fine sampling of the firing train from sear release

ballistics.note: t0 is charge ignition, seconds after sear release

cycle.note: semi, shouldered. carrier_mm rearward travel; bolt_deg 0 locked, 22.5 unlocked; hammer_deg 0 on the sear, positive towards the firing pin, negative overcocked under the carrier; firing_pin_mm forward travel from its rearmost position (primer contact at fp_float); receiver_force_N rearward axial force on the gun body from bore and action, averaged over each sample (a rigid mount would feel this)

recoil.note: Gun pose offsets from rest in the gun frame. z_mm is translation along the bore (negative = rearward). pitch_up_deg and yaw_right_deg rotate the gun about `pivot` (muzzle up / muzzle to the shooter's right, right-handed shooter). support_force_N is the force the gun puts into the support (shoulder plus arms for ads, hands for hip; positive = pushing the shooter back, negative = the arms pulling the gun back as it rebounds), averaged per sample. Semi curves are the single-shot response; because the shooter model is linear, a burst is the sum of shifted copies.

ads.note: shouldered, aimed. Pitch pivot is the buttpad centre; bore axis 41 mm above it (model).

hip.note: unshouldered, held by both hands. Pitch pivot is the firing hand (socket_hand_right).

brass.note: Gun frame. The case is released at socket_eject after it has bounced off the brass deflector; velocity is relative to the gun.

notes: dust cover: opens on the first carrier movement of a closed-cover gun and stays open (as the charge clip does)
last round: the follower lifts the bolt catch and the carrier stops at hold_open_mm on its return instead of closing (manual p. 26); play cycle to max travel, then hold at hold_open_mm

reload from bolt-locked: no charging handle needed; the bolt_catch clip releases the carrier, which runs forward from hold_open_mm (use the cycle curve from where carrier_mm falls through hold_open_mm)
charge clip pulls the carrier 75 mm; the real stroke is to the buffer stop (about 95 mm) and the bolt face must pass the top round at feed_pick_carrier_mm to strip it
